question.question: After an implicit joint configuration is committed and applied by a leader, can rejection of its automatic exit proposal during leadership transfer consume the last application trigger, leaving no implementation-owned retry when that transfer aborts and the same leader remains healthy?
question.importance: A lost automatic-exit continuation can retain outgoing voter requirements and block later configuration changes despite an available quorum; no consensus-safety violation is currently alleged.
contexts: No unrelated client proposals after configuration application
event_paths: Commit implicit joint entry -> initiate transfer -> apply configuration and complete application while transfer active -> automatic proposal rejected -> transfer timeout abort -> continue ordinary ticks and transport

supporting_behavior_ids.B-transfer: Creates the proposal-admission block and clears it on timeout without directly scheduling application.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-replicate: Commits the joint entry and is the consumer of any successful automatic-exit proposal.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-ready: Produces actual application completion; empty Ready batches do not imply another completion.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-node: Shows message/transfer processing can interleave while a Ready awaits Advance.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-authority: A successful new election appends a fresh entry, providing an alternative recovery path.

counterevidence: Successful leadership transfer/new election produces a new leader entry and eventual application trigger.
AutoLeave plus applied/pendingConfIndex and leader guards prevent premature proposals; empty exit entry avoids quota rejection.
Existing TestRawNodeJointAutoLeave covers leadership loss and reacquisition, not same-leader transfer abort.
unknowns: Formal fixed execution and current correspondence must establish complete state-cycle capture and legality; exploration is not Evidence.
question.trigger_rationale: Source narrows retry to real appliedTo calls while transfer timeout only clears a field. This is a specific missing-continuation premise. Contract reading supplies library ownership; a small serialized multi-node execution can now distinguish hidden pending completion from a lost trigger. It is more direct than the separate pending-read/configuration history question.

obligation.description: For an implicit joint configuration already committed and applied, Raft must retain implementation-owned automatic exit continuation when a temporary leadership-transfer admission block ends. Under a stable eligible leader, available joint quorum and continued required caller servicing, it must not remain in a repeatable fair protocol-state cycle that retains the automatic joint configuration without proposing its exit; unrelated client proposals are not a prerequisite.

scope.description: Automatic continuation after transfer abort in a crash-free, fully serviced Raft group.
assumptions: Serialized RawNode calls; successful storage writes precede dependent sends; committed configurations applied before Advance.
Ticks and all surviving network messages are serviced fairly; transfer message loss is finite.
No additional client proposals, leadership changes or snapshots are required after the admitted change.
excluded: Unfair network delivery or stalled caller application

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit and ConfState.AutoLeave assign automatic exit to Raft when safe. AppliedTo implements this by proposing a zero configuration change. Transfer temporarily rejects proposals; timeout ends that block. With committed configuration fully applied, stable leader, available joint quorum and fair execution of required ticks, messages and Ready completion, an exactly repeatable no-progress state cycle retaining AutoLeave contradicts implementation-owned automatic continuation. No numeric exit deadline is inferred.
grounding.applicability: Crash-free synchronous RawNode integration; one admitted implicit joint change, transient dropped transfer TimeoutNow, no remaining transfer and reliable transport thereafter. No obligation for new client proposals or a new election is added.
alternatives: A later applied client entry or new-leader entry can provide another trigger, but neither is owed by the caller in the otherwise quiescent scenario.

bindings.description: Application-completion consumer attempts automatic exit; rejection during transfer leaves AutoLeave installed.

associations.rationale: Binds automatic continuation responsibility to the current consumer and its temporarily blocking authority context.

candidate.rationale: Interface automatic-exit responsibility is grounded; legal prefix and recurrence premise now have exploratory support, subject to fresh fixed execution and correspondence.

rationale: Fix and execute the automatic-continuation obligation. The exploratory driver failure is repaired only by accepting the documented unknown-peer rejection during the later diagnostic phase. Preserve the overlap, comparison and caller duties.

feedback.answered: Exploration reached joint entry index 5 at term 2, started transfer to node 2 with applied=4 and committed=5, applied the joint entry on all three nodes, and dropped an actual TimeoutNow. After abort it observed node 1 still leader, applied=committed=last=5, AutoLeave=true, empty transport queue, and identical captured states across ten serviced tick rounds. A fresh diagnostic proposal then caused leader application of the exit at index 7. The process exited 1 afterward because the driver treated ErrStepPeerNotFound on a removed-peer reply as fatal; no completed rescue event was emitted. These observations remain exploration, not formal Evidence.
remaining: Fresh formal execution of the fixed predicate and driver.
Current checker correspondence: closed-cycle state capture, fair suffix, operation identity and entry/caller legality.
feedback.rationale: Retain both the useful measured prefix and the driver failure. The upcoming fixed check does not retroactively relabel the exploration.
